Test Case Title: Valid credentials return successful login
Test Steps: 1. Send POST /api/login with valid email and password 2. Inspect response
Expected Result: HTTP 200; JSON body contains message "Login successful." and a user object with id and email

Test Case Title: Missing email field is rejected
Test Steps: 1. Send POST /api/login with only password field
Expected Result: HTTP 400; message "Email and password are required."; no DB query attempted

Test Case Title: Missing password field is rejected
Test Steps: 1. Send POST /api/login with only email field
Expected Result: HTTP 400; message "Email and password are required."

Test Case Title: Both fields missing are rejected
Test Steps: 1. Send POST /api/login with empty body {}
Expected Result: HTTP 400; message "Email and password are required."

Test Case Title: Empty-string fields are treated as missing
Test Steps: 1. Send POST /api/login with email="" and password=""
Expected Result: HTTP 400 (empty strings must not pass the required-field check)

Test Case Title: Malformed email format is rejected before DB lookup
Test Steps: 1. Send POST /api/login with a non-email string in the email field
Expected Result: HTTP 400 before any database lookup, per API and Data Mapping validation rules (GAP: current code only checks truthiness, not format - expect FAIL until format validation is added)

Test Case Title: Wrong password for an existing user is rejected
Test Steps: 1. Send POST /api/login with correct email, wrong password
Expected Result: HTTP 401; message "Invalid email or password."

Test Case Title: Non-existent email returns same generic error as wrong password
Test Steps: 1. Send POST /api/login with an email not present in the user table
Expected Result: HTTP 401 with the identical generic message used for wrong-password (no user-enumeration difference)

Test Case Title: Validation errors (400) are distinguishable from auth errors (401)
Test Steps: 1. Trigger a missing-field request 2. Trigger a wrong-credentials request 3. Compare status codes
Expected Result: First request returns 400, second returns 401, so the frontend can render different messages for each case

Test Case Title: Successful login response never exposes the password field
Test Steps: 1. Send a valid login request 2. Inspect full JSON response body
Expected Result: Response `user` object contains only id and email; no password or password hash present anywhere in the payload

Test Case Title: SQL injection payloads in login fields do not authenticate or crash the server
Test Steps: 1. Send POST /api/login with a SQL-injection style payload in the email field
Expected Result: HTTP 401 (not 200, not 500); server does not error or return unrelated user rows, confirming parameterized queries are effective

Test Case Title: Malformed JSON request body is handled gracefully
Test Steps: 1. Send POST /api/login with a body that is not valid JSON and Content-Type: application/json
Expected Result: Server responds with a 400-level error, not an unhandled exception or raw stack trace

Test Case Title: Database outage returns a generic 503 instead of leaking internals
Test Steps: 1. Stop/point backend at unreachable DB 2. Send a valid-looking login request
Expected Result: HTTP 503; message "Database request failed. Verify the database server and backend environment settings."; no raw driver error/stack trace exposed

Test Case Title: Passwords are not compared or stored as plain text
Test Steps: 1. Inspect the `user` table password column and the login comparison logic
Expected Result: Password is stored hashed (e.g., bcrypt) and compared via hash verification, not a plain-text SQL equality check (GAP: current implementation compares plain text - expect FAIL until hashing is introduced)

Test Case Title: Successful login issues a session identifier or token
Test Steps: 1. Send a valid login request 2. Inspect response body/headers for a session id, token, or Set-Cookie header
Expected Result: Response includes a session identifier or signed token that can be used to access protected routes (GAP: not implemented yet - expect FAIL until DT-34 lands)

Test Case Title: Leading/trailing whitespace in email is trimmed before lookup
Test Steps: 1. Send POST /api/login with extra spaces around the email value
Expected Result: HTTP 200; login succeeds identically to the untrimmed value

Test Case Title: Unauthenticated request to a protected product endpoint is rejected
Test Steps: 1. Send GET /api/products (or current /api/bootstrap/tables) with no Authorization header/session cookie
Expected Result: HTTP 401 (GAP: no product routes or auth middleware exist yet - expect FAIL until Phase 3 + DT-34 land)

Test Case Title: Authenticated request with a valid session/token reaches product data
Test Steps: 1. Log in to obtain a token/session 2. Send GET /api/products with that credential attached
Expected Result: HTTP 200 with product list data

Test Case Title: Invalid or expired token on a protected endpoint is rejected
Test Steps: 1. Send GET /api/products with a garbage or expired token value
Expected Result: HTTP 401

Test Case Title: Auth middleware is applied consistently across all product endpoints
Test Steps: 1. Repeat TC-017 against GET, POST, PUT /products/:id, and DELETE /products/:id
Expected Result: All four verbs return 401 without valid credentials - none are left open (Migration Plan explicitly warns against opening any endpoint before DT-34 lands)

Test Case Title: CORS only allows the configured client origin
Preconditions: Backend running with configured client origin env var
Test Steps: 1. Send a request with an Origin header that does not match the configured client origin 2. Inspect Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header
Expected Result: CORS headers do not reflect a wildcard (*) or the disallowed origin back to the caller

Test Case Title: Login page renders required fields and controls
Test Steps: 1. Navigate to /login 2. Inspect the DOM
Expected Result: Page shows an email input, a password input, and a submit button labeled Login

Test Case Title: Password field masks input
Test Steps: 1. Type a value into the password field 2. Inspect the rendered input
Expected Result: Characters are masked (input type=password), not shown in plain text

Test Case Title: Empty form submission is blocked client-side
Test Steps: 1. Leave email and password blank 2. Click Login
Expected Result: Browser native required-field validation prevents submission; no network request is sent

Test Case Title: Valid login redirects user to the product page
Test Steps: seeded user exists
Expected Result: email=admin@apple.com, password=admin
Priority: Login request succeeds and the app navigates to /products automatically

Test Case Title: Invalid credentials show an inline error without navigating away
Test Steps: 1. Enter a wrong password 2. Click Login
Expected Result: User remains on /login; an inline error message (from the 401 response) is displayed; no crash or blank page

Test Case Title: Backend unreachable shows a distinct network-error message
Test Steps: 1. Enter valid-looking credentials 2. Click Login while backend is down
Expected Result: Inline message reads "Unable to reach the backend. Check the API server and try again." (distinct from an invalid-credentials message)

Test Case Title: Submit control shows a loading state and prevents double-submit
Test Steps: 1. Click Login 2. Immediately attempt to click Login again before the response returns
Expected Result: Button text changes to "Signing In..." and is disabled for the duration of the request, so a second submission cannot be triggered

Test Case Title: Previous error message clears on a new submit attempt
Preconditions: An error is currently displayed from a prior failed attempt
Test Steps: 1. Trigger an invalid-credentials error 2. Correct the credentials and click Login again
Test Data: First: wrong password. Then: email=admin@apple.com, password=admin
Expected Result: The old error message is cleared/replaced once the new submission starts, not left stale on screen

Test Case Title: Login form does not ship with real credentials pre-filled
Preconditions: App loaded at /login on a production build
Test Steps: 1. Load /login fresh 2. Inspect the default values of the email and password inputs
Expected Result: Fields are empty by default (GAP: current build pre-fills email=admin@apple.com and password=admin as default state, which should not ship to production - expect FAIL until removed)

Test Case Title: Successful login auto-redirects without manual navigation
Test Steps: 1. Log in with valid credentials 2. Observe URL/route after submission
Expected Result: Browser URL changes to /products without any further user action

Test Case Title: Already-authenticated user visiting /login is redirected to /products
Preconditions: User is currently logged in (in-memory state set)
Test Steps: 1. While authenticated, navigate directly to /login
Expected Result: App immediately redirects to /products instead of showing the login form

Test Case Title: Unauthenticated user cannot reach /products via direct URL
Test Steps: 1. With no active session, navigate directly to /products
Expected Result: App redirects to /login instead of rendering product data

Test Case Title: Authenticated session survives a full page refresh
Preconditions: User has just logged in successfully
Test Steps: 1. Log in 2. Confirm /products is showing 3. Perform a full browser refresh (F5) 4. Observe resulting route
Expected Result: User remains on /products after refresh (GAP: current auth state lives only in React memory and is lost on refresh, bouncing the user back to /login - expect FAIL until DT-34 persists a session/token)

Test Case Title: Logout clears session and blocks further product access
Preconditions: User is logged in and viewing /products
Test Steps: 1. Click Log Out 2. Attempt to navigate back to /products
Expected Result: User is redirected to /login on logout, and re-visiting /products afterward also redirects to /login (no residual access)

Test Case Title: Unknown route falls back based on auth state
Test Steps: 1. Navigate to an undefined path such as /does-not-exist
Expected Result: Authenticated users land on /products; unauthenticated users land on /login - no blank page or unhandled route error

Test Case Title: Route files contain no inline SQL or business logic
Test Steps: 1. Inspect backend/src/routes/authRoutes.js (and future product routes) 2. Confirm they only wire HTTP verbs to controller functions
Expected Result: Route files delegate to controllers/services; no raw SQL or validation logic embedded directly in route definitions

Test Case Title: No hardcoded database credentials or secrets in source
Test Steps: 1. Inspect backend/src/config/env.js and related files for hardcoded host/user/password values
Expected Result: All connection settings are read from environment variables (env.dbHost, env.dbUser, etc.); no literal credentials committed to source, avoiding the legacy config.php duplication issue

Test Case Title: API error responses use a consistent JSON shape
Test Steps: 1. Trigger a 400 response, a 401 response, and a 503 response 2. Compare response body shapes
Expected Result: Every error response is a JSON object with a `message` string field, with no inconsistent shapes across endpoints

Test Case Title: No leftover debug/console statements in committed source
Preconditions: Frontend and backend source available for review
Test Steps: 1. Search backend/src and frontend/src for console.log/console.debug calls not tied to intentional error logging
Expected Result: No stray debug output left in committed login-flow code

Test Case Title: Product data shown after login matches backend data
Test Steps: user logged in
Test Data: 1. Log in 2. Compare each row shown in the product table on /products against the raw rows in the `product` table/API response
Expected Result: N/A
Priority: Displayed product_id, product_name, price, and quantity values match the backend data exactly, with correct number formatting
